answer: One voice, one identity: a certified voice-biometrics centre enrols the operator's voiceprint and signs each epoch challenge binding that print to the agent's key, re-checked every epoch. A second key claiming the same print is rejected outright — the centre, not the claimant, holds the template. Faking 1,000 identities needs 1,000 distinct voices at roughly $40 each in supervised enrolment, about $40,000, plus a fresh spoken cipher no recording can replay — liveness checks sift the nebula of synthetic voices from the ocean of genuine calls, revoking any spoofed template at once.
